notes: either … or is read as one correlative pair on the single אוֹ, headed on the closing or (rule 14), rather than leaving either added; no other morpheme in the clause is itself what either says.

A competing division would give shall make to the verb and special to the infinitive לִנְדֹּר; the light-verb reading was taken because פלא is what special renders and the infinitive is what the noun vow renders (rule 44).
The לְ of לִנְדֹּר is unrepresented because the ASV writes no function word before the verbal noun vow (rules 40, 52).
